top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Russia struck Ukraine's biggest Danube grain port on Thursday, a day after Ukrainian drones knocked two terminals out of action at Novorossiysk - the two sides are now systematically dismantling each other's food exports, and wheat futures moved on it. The war's human cost hardened too: UN monitors counted 437 Ukrainian civilians killed in July, the worst month since May 2022. The Middle East pulled the other way, with Israeli troops moving into a West Bank village to break a settler siege that Washington's own ambassador called "terror", while Iran and the US traded competing claims over who controls the Strait of Hormuz. Watch the grain lane: if Black Sea and Danube ports stay under fire, the price shows up in bread long before it shows up in headlines.

stories.headline: Russia strikes Ukraine's largest Danube grain port as Zelensky presses US for Patriots
stories.summary: Russia struck Ukraine's biggest grain export port on the Danube on Thursday, causing damage and starting a fire, Ukrainian authorities said. It came after President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine needs about 5 per cent of US Patriot interceptor stocks to protect its cities through winter. Damage assessments are Ukrainian accounts; Moscow did not comment on the strike.

stories.headline: Ukrainian attack on Novorossiysk grain terminals lifts wheat futures
stories.summary: Two grain terminals at Novorossiysk, Russia's largest Black Sea export port, halted work after a Ukrainian drone attack, and EU and Chicago wheat futures rose in response. Russian officials reported casualties at the port; the figures are Russian accounts and have not been independently verified. Grain exports from both countries are falling as each strikes the other's shipping facilities.

stories.headline: UN says July was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since May 2022
stories.summary: At least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine during July, the highest monthly toll since May 2022, according to a UN human rights monitoring report. The UN attributes the rise largely to long-range strikes on cities away from the front line.

stories.headline: Israel sends troops into West Bank village besieged by settlers; US envoy calls siege 'terror'
stories.summary: Israel dispatched more troops to Qusra, near Nablus, where settlers have blockaded Palestinian homes since 9 August. Residents say they were cut off from food, water and power; the village mayor said six homes were evacuated and taken over by Israeli soldiers. The US ambassador to Israel publicly described the siege as 'terror'.

stories.headline: Israel ties Lebanon withdrawal to Hezbollah disarmament after US criticism
stories.summary: Israel's defence minister said Israeli forces will not withdraw from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed, qualifying remarks a day earlier that had suggested an indefinite occupation and drew criticism from Washington. Beirut has separately accused Israel of systematic destruction of property in the south; Israel says it is acting against militant infrastructure.

stories.headline: Iran and US make competing claims over control of the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Tehran said the Strait of Hormuz is effectively under its control and that it intends to impose a toll system, after President Donald Trump said the United States would 'keep' control of the waterway. Both statements are claims by parties to the conflict and neither has been independently verified. The strait has been shut since the US operation against Iran began on 28 February.

stories.headline: Putin visits disputed Kuril Islands; Japan's PM calls it 'absolutely unacceptable'
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin made what Russian state media described as his first visit to the Kuril Islands, which Japan claims as its Northern Territories. Tokyo lodged a formal protest and Japan's prime minister called the trip absolutely unacceptable. Russia has held the islands since 1945 and the dispute has blocked a post-war peace treaty between the two countries.

stories.headline: Turkey sets out plans for a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Ankara laid out how it envisages the defence pact signed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, following the 'Mecca Joint Defence Agreement' the three concluded on 7 August. The grouping brings together two of Washington's Sunni Muslim allies and a nuclear-armed state, and is being watched closely for what it means for the regional balance with Iran.

stories.headline: Air India orders drug tests for all pilots after mid-air plunge
stories.summary: Air India will require drug testing for every pilot following a mid-air altitude loss on one of its flights, the airline said. The measure goes beyond India's existing random-testing regime and comes as the carrier remains under regulatory scrutiny.

stories.headline: US inflation slowed slightly in July despite elevated fuel prices
stories.summary: US consumer price growth eased a little in July even with fuel costs still high, official data showed, and US stocks closed mostly higher on the reading. Energy prices remain elevated because of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Colombia's president pledges reconstruction fund as quake search enters critical phase
stories.summary: President de la Espriella announced a reconstruction fund as rescue teams entered what officials called the critical window for finding survivors of Colombia's earthquake. A woman was pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after the quake.

stories.headline: WHO chief says Congo's Ebola outbreak is on track to be the deadliest ever
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is on track to eclipse the 2014-16 West African epidemic, which killed more than 11,000 people. The outbreak was declared on 15 May and there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this Ebola species.

stories.headline: Trump's press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave the White House
stories.summary: President Trump said White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will step down from her post. No successor was named at the time of the announcement.

stories.headline: Meta says it has removed 756,000 Australian teen accounts before under-16 ban
stories.summary: Meta said it has taken down 756,000 accounts belonging to Australian teenagers as enforcement of the country's under-16 social media ban approaches. The figure is Meta's own, and regulators have not published an independent count.

stories.headline: Taiwan says it was targeted last month in an AI-driven hacking campaign
stories.summary: Taiwanese authorities said the island was hit in July by a hacking campaign that used AI tooling to accelerate intrusions. Taipei's account has not been independently corroborated and no attribution was confirmed publicly at the time of reporting.

stories.headline: UK defends seizing shadow-fleet tanker after Putin threat
stories.summary: The UK government said it is 'disrupting and deterring shadow fleet vessels' in accordance with the law, after Vladimir Putin threatened a response to Britain's seizure of a tanker linked to the sanctions-evading fleet that carries Russian oil.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Workers' Party chief Pritam Singh was struck off the roll of lawyers on Thursday, with the Court of Three Judges finding that his conviction for giving false evidence to a parliamentary committee involved dishonesty and left no room for a lesser sanction. The money news is friendlier - more than 2.4 million adult Singaporeans will get S$400 to S$600 in cash from 9 September under the enhanced cost-of-living payment. Scams ran through most of the rest of the day: police are investigating 270 people over $5.4 million in losses, and six men were charged over a moneylending syndicate tied to more than 25,000 ScamShield reports. Separately, a warning went out about Telegram accounts hijacked through fake transport-voucher links. The talk is seventh-month flavoured this week, from Hungry Ghost advisories to a festival AR game in the CBD. If you expect the September payout, check that your bank details with the Government are current now, not in three weeks.

stories.headline: Pritam Singh struck off the roll of lawyers
stories.summary: The Court of Three Judges struck Workers' Party chief Pritam Singh off the roll of advocates and solicitors after he did not contest the Law Society's application. Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon said it was not disputed that his offences of giving false evidence to a parliamentary committee involved dishonesty, and did not meet the high threshold for an exception to being struck off.

stories.headline: Over 2.4 million Singaporeans to get up to S$600 cash from 9 September
stories.summary: More than 2.4 million adult Singaporeans will receive a one-off payment of S$400 to S$600 under the Enhanced Cost-of-Living Special Payment from 9 September. It goes to adult Singaporeans living in Singapore with assessable income of up to S$100,000 who own no more than one property.

stories.headline: Chan Chun Sing: Singapore plans 'just in case', not 'just in time'
stories.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing said Singapore deliberately builds buffers into food, energy and supply-chain planning rather than optimising for efficiency alone, describing it as a 'just in case' rather than 'just in time' approach to strategic vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: 270 people under police investigation over scams costing victims $5.4 million
stories.summary: Police said 270 people are being investigated for suspected involvement in scams in which victims lost about $5.4 million. The figure is from the Singapore Police Force.

stories.headline: Six men charged over alleged unlicensed moneylending syndicate
stories.summary: Six men were charged in connection with an alleged unlicensed moneylending syndicate that police say is linked to at least 25,500 ScamShield reports and at least 1,509 police reports, of which 883 related to unlicensed moneylending.

stories.headline: Police warn of Telegram accounts hijacked via fake transport-voucher links
stories.summary: The police issued a warning after Telegram accounts were compromised through fake public transport voucher links. Victims who entered their details on the phishing pages had their accounts taken over and used to spread the scam further.

stories.headline: More than 500 fake websites impersonating MHA and Home Team agencies taken down
stories.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs said more than 500 fake websites impersonating MHA and Home Team agencies have been taken down. Investigations so far showed no evidence the sites were used to run scams or phish for information from the public.

stories.headline: Bomb hoax forces evacuation at Xinmin Secondary School
stories.summary: Students and staff at Xinmin Secondary School were evacuated after a bomb threat. Police and school personnel checked the premises and found no suspicious items; classes resumed the same morning and police are investigating the false threat.

stories.headline: Singaporean man and woman rescued from kidnappers in Johor; man wanted by CNB
stories.summary: Malaysian police rescued a 32-year-old Singaporean man and a 33-year-old Singaporean woman from an alleged kidnapping ring. The Singapore Police Force said the man had no valid travel document, is wanted by the Central Narcotics Bureau and is believed to know one of the alleged kidnappers.

stories.headline: Malaysian man caught at Woodlands with fake staff passes bearing Supreme Court and MHA emblems
stories.summary: A 23-year-old Malaysian man was stopped at Woodlands Checkpoint allegedly carrying fake employee passes and official-looking stamps bearing the emblems of the Supreme Court and the Ministry of Home Affairs. Authorities linked the items to scam activity and said he would be charged.

stories.headline: Couple arrested after drugs found in flat with a toddler and a baby
stories.summary: A couple were arrested after the Central Narcotics Bureau found drugs at their home, where their sons aged three years and seven months were in the master bedroom. Both children were placed in the care of relatives.

stories.headline: SAF regular siphoned S$1.6 million from his father, including S$533,800 in CPF funds
stories.summary: A Singapore Armed Forces regular, Tay Yi Cong, siphoned S$1.6 million from his father, including S$533,800 in CPF funds. The court heard that after his 62-year-old father noticed the falling balances, Tay posed as bank officers to delay discovery and pretended to file a police report on his behalf.

stories.headline: Eight men arrested over theft of marine gas oil from a tugboat off Tuas
stories.summary: Eight men were arrested over the alleged theft of marine gas oil from a tugboat in waters off Tuas, police said.

stories.headline: Man, 26, to be charged over unlicensed massage shops and a separate fire
stories.summary: A 26-year-old man will be charged with allegedly operating massage establishments without valid licences, and separately with causing a fire in an unrelated incident.

stories.headline: PM Wong sends condolences to China over death of former premier Zhu Rongji
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong sent condolences to Beijing following the death of former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji, who served from 1998 to 2003 and died of illness on Wednesday at the age of 97. Zhu was closely associated with the reforms that opened China's economy.

stories.headline: Singapore-registered container ship crashes into riverbank in India; MPA investigating
stories.summary: A Singapore-registered container ship struck a riverbank in India, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said it will investigate the incident.

stories.headline: Singapore Red Cross pledges $50,000 each to quake-hit Colombia and to Venezuela
stories.summary: The Singapore Red Cross pledged $50,000 in aid for earthquake-hit Colombia and a further $50,000 for Venezuela, where an El Nino-driven power and water crisis is deepening.

stories.headline: Johor Bahru hospital sees surge in Singaporeans using MediSave
stories.summary: Regency Specialist Hospital in Johor Bahru reports a surge in Singaporean patients paying with MediSave. About 90 per cent of them are women, with maternity-related care among the most common treatments.

stories.headline: Royal Caribbean to base Navigator of the Seas in Singapore year-round from October
stories.summary: Royal Caribbean will extend Navigator of the Seas' Singapore season to a full year from October, giving the port a year-round large-ship homeport deployment.

stories.headline: NEA advisory for Hungry Ghost Festival: clear offerings after prayers
stories.summary: The National Environment Agency reminded the public to clear offerings after prayers during the Hungry Ghost Festival, saying items left behind may constitute littering. Burning should be done in designated containers.

stories.headline: Hungry Ghost Festival event in the CBD brings an AR game and spooky storytelling
stories.summary: A Hungry Ghost Festival event running in the CBD from 13 August to 10 September features an immersive augmented-reality game and storytelling sessions built around the seventh-month traditions.

stories.headline: Aaron Kwok spotted with his family at Universal Studios and the zoo
stories.summary: Fans spotted Hong Kong star Aaron Kwok, 60, at Universal Studios Singapore and the Singapore Zoo, where he was seen spending time with his family.

stories.headline: Yoasobi to headline the National Stadium in February 2027
stories.summary: Japanese duo Yoasobi will play a Southeast Asia-exclusive concert at Singapore's National Stadium in February 2027, becoming the first Japanese act to headline the venue.

stories.headline: National coach Gavin Lee and Irfan Fandi back anti-scalping campaign
stories.summary: Singapore football head coach Gavin Lee and player Irfan Fandi lent their support to an anti-scalping campaign after tickets for the Singapore versus Thailand fixture were resold at marked-up prices.

stories.headline: Singapore's street ice cream vendors say they will keep going 'as long' as they can
stories.summary: Street ice cream vendors, a fixture along Orchard Road and outside malls, told Mothership they intend to keep selling for as long as they are able, even as ageing hawkers and rising costs raise questions about how long the trade will last.

stories.headline: Employer says her helper became uncontactable after a paid trip home
stories.summary: A 37-year-old Singaporean woman said she booked and paid for her domestic helper's two-way flight to visit a sick mother, and that the helper became uncontactable afterwards. The account is the employer's; the helper's side has not been reported.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: The grain corridor has become the main front in Ukraine: Russia hit the Danube port of Izmail on Thursday, days after Ukrainian drones stopped two terminals at Novorossiysk, so both sides are now attacking the other's ability to export food rather than each other's armies. Away from the ports the war is getting deadlier for civilians, with the UN logging 437 killed in July, the worst month in more than four years, while Zelensky says he needs about 5 per cent of America's Patriot stock to get through winter. Lebanon is the theatre that shifted: Israel's defence minister now ties any withdrawal to Hezbollah disarming, hardening a position that had already drawn US criticism. Gaza, by contrast, is quieter than it has been in months - Thursday's strike was the first fatality there in over a week. Whether that lull survives depends less on Gaza than on what happens across the northern border.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: The grain corridor is now the main front - Russia hit Ukraine's largest Danube export port on Aug 13, days after Ukrainian drones stopped two terminals at Novorossiysk, while UN monitors record the deadliest month for civilians since May 2022

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It has since seized parts of the east and south, and front lines have been largely static for long stretches.
Ukraine's general staff says its forces hit Russia's Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries overnight, causing fires at both. Local authorities in Krasnodar confirmed a fire.
Zelensky says Russian forces killed six people in a pre-dawn attack on Zaporizhzhia that he says involved North Korean ballistic missiles. This is a Ukrainian claim; Moscow has not commented.
Zelensky says Ukraine has given US negotiators its own written proposals for ending the war. The terms were not disclosed and Moscow has not responded publicly.

Two grain terminals at Novorossiysk, Russia's largest Black Sea export port, halt work after a Ukrainian drone attack that also targeted the naval base there. Russian officials say three people were killed, including a child; the toll is a Russian account. Chicago wheat futures rose about 3%.
Russia says Ukrainian strikes on its grain and agricultural infrastructure are pushing up global food prices. Kyiv has not responded to the accusation.
Zelensky says Ukraine needs about 5% of US Patriot interceptor stocks to protect its cities through the coming winter.
The Kiel Institute reports that military aid to Ukraine surged in June, driven largely by the EU's new Ukraine Support Loan, while warning of persistent long-term shortfalls.
Ukrainian farmers say Russia's Black Sea blockade has trapped their harvest, leaving grain unsold as both sides strike each other's export infrastructure.
Putin visits the Japan-claimed Kuril Islands, prompting a formal protest from Tokyo. Russia has held the islands since 1945 and the dispute has blocked a post-war peace treaty.

A Russian military officer is killed by a bomb in Russian-annexed Crimea. The regional governor says a woman was arrested on suspicion of assassinating him for Ukrainian special services; this is a Russian official account and Kyiv has not commented.
The UK defends its seizure of a shadow-fleet tanker after a threat from Putin, saying it is 'disrupting and deterring shadow fleet vessels' in accordance with the law.
UN human rights monitors report at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July, the highest monthly toll since May 2022.
Russia strikes Ukraine's largest grain export port on the Danube, causing damage and starting a fire, Ukrainian authorities say.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Frozen but noisier - Washington and Tehran each claim the strait on Aug 13, Iran is looking to BRICS finance to work around sanctions, and the waterway remains shut

timeline.event: The US military operation against Iran begins; Tehran effectively blockades the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world's oil normally passes.
President Trump says he has cancelled planned strikes on Iran, conditional on a deal being made 'rapidly'.
The UAE says a 'hostile Iranian attack' struck an Adnoc-affiliated tanker with a missile in the strait, with no casualties. Iran has not publicly confirmed the account.
The International Energy Agency cuts its 2026 global oil demand forecast again, citing the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

A person briefed on the matter says a credible missile threat prompted the Secret Service to move President Trump onto an unmarked jet out of Turkey, while cabinet members remained aboard a decoy aircraft.

Iran says the Strait of Hormuz is effectively under its control and that it intends to impose a toll system, after Trump said the US would 'keep' control of the waterway. Both are claims by parties to the conflict and neither has been independently verified.
Iran's central bank governor says the country will join the BRICS development bank soon, as Tehran looks for financing routes around international sanctions.
Turkey lays out plans for the defence pact it signed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on Aug 7, a grouping being watched for what it changes about the regional balance with Iran.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Gaza is quieter than it has been - Aug 13's strike was the first fatality in over a week - while Lebanon hardens, with Israel now tying any withdrawal to Hezbollah disarming

timeline.event: Hamas agrees a disarmament deal as part of a wider Gaza roadmap; analysts note the plan faces significant obstacles.
Netanyahu tells a cabinet meeting that 'Israel rejects the 15-point document' and that the military will carry out no withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed.
Settlers begin blockading Palestinian homes in the West Bank village of Qusra, near Nablus. Residents say they are cut off from food, water and power.
Israeli security forces intervene against the settlers at Qusra, then reportedly withdraw, with about a dozen settlers said to remain at the site.

Israel sends more troops into Qusra and into Palestinian homes there. The village mayor says six homes were evacuated and taken over by Israeli soldiers. The US ambassador to Israel publicly calls the settler siege 'terror'.
An Israeli airstrike kills a Palestinian man in Gaza, the first fatality there in over a week, medics say, as the Israeli military scales back targeted attacks under US pressure.
Israel's defence minister says Israel will not withdraw from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed, qualifying remarks a day earlier that suggested indefinite occupation and drew US criticism.

Doctors say the death rate among Gaza cancer patients is rising amid Israeli restrictions on medical transfers. Israel says its curbs are security-driven; the two accounts have not been independently reconciled.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: WHO's director-general now says the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is on track to become the deadliest ever recorded - the toll has roughly doubled in three weeks, and there is still no licensed vaccine or treatment for this Ebola species, though trials have been authorised in Canada and the UK. Bangladesh is carrying two epidemics at once: a measles wave that has been killing about five children a day since March, and a dengue season running at near-record hospitalisations. The Americas are having their worst measles year in 22 years, although PAHO's regional data is now about a month old, so the real position is likely worse than it reads. Practical takeaway: check your MMR status before travelling to South Asia or Central America.

outbreaks.name: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) - DR Congo & Uganda
outbreaks.status: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record and the largest ever in DR Congo; WHO says it is on track to eclipse the 2014-16 West African epidemic. No approved vaccine or treatment exists for this Ebola species.
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases and deaths, DR Congo and Uganda combined, data as of 9 Aug 2026 from WHO AFRO's Bundibugyo virus disease external situation report 13 (CFR 45.9%); Ituri province accounts for 85.8% of cases and 80.6% of deaths. WHO's last formal Disease Outbreak News (2026-DON614, 1 Aug) put the figure at 3,626 confirmed cases and 1,589 deaths as of 30 Jul, and also counted one imported case in France plus two DRC-diagnosed patients treated in Germany. DRC authorities reported 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths as of 11 Aug; that newer number is not yet WHO-ratified.

outbreaks.name: Measles - Bangladesh
outbreaks.status: Large national outbreak running since March; deaths still accruing at roughly five a day
outbreaks.scope_note: Bangladesh DGHS figures as of 8am on 13 Aug 2026, reported by The Business Standard and The Daily Star: 17,543 laboratory-confirmed cases and 140,076 suspected cases; 890 combined deaths, of which 99 are laboratory-confirmed and 791 suspected. Since 15 March, 121,908 suspected measles patients have been hospitalised and 117,690 have recovered.

outbreaks.name: Measles - Americas Region
outbreaks.status: Worst measles year in the Americas in 22 years; PAHO issued a regional epidemiological alert on 7 Aug
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases reported across the Americas through epidemiological week 28, ending 18 Jul 2026, per PAHO's epidemiological alert of 7 Aug (announced 8 Aug). The 44 deaths were reported by three countries; Guatemala accounts for 30,371 cases and 26 deaths and Mexico for 12,255 cases and 17 deaths, with Guatemala, Mexico, the US and Peru together making up 95% of cases. Note the underlying data are now about a month old - PAHO had not published a newer regional count at the time of this brief.

outbreaks.name: Dengue - Bangladesh
outbreaks.status: Peak-season transmission; hospitalisations at record levels and deaths climbing through August
outbreaks.scope_note: Hospitalised dengue cases and deaths reported nationwide in 2026 through 8am on 13 Aug by Bangladesh's Directorate General of Health Services, as relayed by The Daily Star; 1,615 patients were in hospital. The Business Standard reported the DGHS count at 21,550 cases and 63 deaths a day earlier, consistent with this trajectory.

stories.headline: WHO chief says Congo's Ebola outbreak is on track to be the deadliest ever recorded
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, declared on 15 May, is on track to eclipse the 2014-16 West African epidemic that killed more than 11,000 people. WHO AFRO's situation report puts confirmed deaths at 2,011 as of 9 August, a case fatality ratio of 45.9 per cent.

stories.headline: UN says Ebola deaths have passed 2,000, with half of them in the last 20 days
stories.summary: UN News reported that DRC officials counted more than 2,000 deaths and over 4,000 confirmed cases as of 11 August, with about half the deaths recorded in the preceding 20 days. Vaccine trials have been authorised in Canada and the UK but results are months away, and treatment trials are running in Ituri province. The DRC-reported figures are ahead of WHO's last formal Disease Outbreak News.

stories.headline: Bangladesh measles deaths reach 890 as five more children die in 24 hours
stories.summary: Five more children died with measles or measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on 13 August, taking Bangladesh's combined confirmed and suspected measles death toll to 890, according to DGHS data. The agency also logged 951 new suspected cases and 74 new laboratory-confirmed infections in the same period.
stories.source: The Business Standard, The Daily Star

stories.headline: Bangladesh dengue toll rises to 65 as hospitalisations stay near record levels
stories.summary: Two more dengue patients died and 693 were hospitalised in the 24 hours to 8am on 13 August, taking Bangladesh's 2026 death toll to 65 and total cases to 22,243, the DGHS said. Both deaths were in the two Dhaka city corporation areas, and 1,615 patients remain in hospital.
stories.source: The Daily Star, The Business Standard

stories.headline: PAHO alert: the Americas record their worst measles year in 22 years
stories.summary: PAHO issued a regional epidemiological alert urging countries to strengthen vaccination, surveillance and outbreak response, after the Americas logged 47,459 confirmed measles cases through epidemiological week 28 - more than three times the 15,011 recorded in all of 2025. Forty-four deaths have been reported across three countries.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch SharePoint first: a Rapid7 proof-of-concept for CVE-2026-55040, an authentication bypass Microsoft fixed back in July, was weaponised the same day it was published and is now being used in attacks. Adobe is the other emergency - a critical authorisation bug in Commerce and Magento (CVE-2026-71362) lets an unauthenticated attacker take over a customer's session, and Sansec was already blocking attempts before the advisory landed. Past those two, the cycle is about things already inside the network: Lazarus burned a Windows WinSock driver zero-day that CISA has since added to its exploited catalogue, and Cisco firewalls, VMware vCenter and Fortinet gear are all being exploited alongside it. The AI supply-chain tail keeps growing, from poisoned LiteLLM releases to malicious MCP servers that talk coding agents into leaking secrets. Order of work: internet-facing SharePoint, then Adobe Commerce, then Cisco ASA, then everything else.

stories.headline: 'City-Forum' data-theft campaign targets Salesforce and ServiceNow customer portals
stories.summary: A threat cluster tracked as City-Forum is abusing misconfigured Salesforce and ServiceNow customer portals to pull records out of tenants without exploiting a product vulnerability. Defenders should review guest-user and public-record permissions on both platforms rather than waiting for a patch.

stories.headline: Android malware pair takes out loans in victims' names and relays their credit cards
stories.summary: Researchers describe an Android malware combination that goes beyond credential theft: it applies for loans in the victim's name and relays NFC card data to an attacker-controlled device for in-person payments. Distribution is via sideloaded apps outside Google Play.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit critical Adobe Commerce flaw to hijack customer accounts
stories.summary: An incorrect-authorisation flaw in Adobe Commerce, Commerce B2B and Magento lets an unauthenticated attacker switch a customer session to another account, with no existing account, admin privileges or user interaction required. Adobe said it was unaware of exploitation when it issued the advisory, but Sansec reported its WAF was already blocking attempts. NVD scores it 9.1 (CRITICAL). Patch supported release branches now.

stories.headline: Lazarus exploited a Windows zero-day to gain SYSTEM and deploy a backdoor at defence firms
stories.summary: North Korea-linked Lazarus used a use-after-free in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock to elevate to SYSTEM and install a backdoor on targets in the defence sector. Microsoft patched it in the August rollup and CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August. NVD scores it 7.0 (HIGH) as a local privilege escalation.
stories.source: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: 737 Chrome VPN extensions caught routing user traffic through third-party proxies
stories.summary: Researchers found 737 Chrome extensions marketed as VPNs that silently route users' browsing through proxy infrastructure they do not control, effectively turning installs into residential exit nodes. Check installed extensions and remove any from the published list.

stories.headline: SharePoint authentication bypass weaponised within hours of a public PoC
stories.summary: A JWT-validation weakness in Microsoft SharePoint lets an unauthenticated attacker impersonate users or administrators, disclosing files and modifying data. Microsoft patched it in July and CISA warned defenders on 15 July; attacks began the same day Rapid7 published a technical write-up and proof-of-concept on 12 August. NVD scores it 9.1 (CRITICAL). Patch internet-facing SharePoint first.

stories.headline: API flaw lets weaker AI models decode stronger models' reasoning traces
stories.summary: Researchers report that a design flaw in how OpenAI, Anthropic and Google expose model outputs allows a cheaper model to reconstruct portions of a stronger model's hidden reasoning, leaking information the providers intend to withhold. There is no CVE; treat it as an information-disclosure risk when reasoning traces are considered sensitive.

stories.headline: Adobe patches three CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic
stories.summary: Adobe shipped fixes for three maximum-severity vulnerabilities across ColdFusion and Campaign Classic, all rated CVSS 10.0 by the vendor and allowing code execution on affected servers. No exploitation had been reported at publication, but ColdFusion is a recurring target - patch on the same cycle as Adobe Commerce.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit a VMware vCenter vulnerability for persistent remote access
stories.summary: Intrusions are using a vCenter flaw to establish persistent remote access to virtualisation management planes, giving attackers control over hosted workloads. vCenter should not be internet-reachable; verify patch level and audit for unexpected accounts and scheduled tasks.

stories.headline: Malicious LiteLLM releases tied to the Trivy hack may have exposed 2,100+ organisations
stories.summary: Poisoned releases of the LiteLLM package, linked to the earlier compromise of the Trivy scanner project, may have reached more than 2,100 organisations. Anyone who pulled LiteLLM in the affected window should rotate API keys and check for outbound connections from build agents.

stories.headline: SAP Commerce Cloud flaw could let unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary code
stories.summary: A vulnerability in SAP Commerce Cloud allows unauthenticated remote code execution against exposed instances. SAP has issued a fix; apply it and restrict administrative endpoints to trusted networks.

stories.headline: 'ShieldBreak' PoC claims a Microsoft Defender patch bypass granting SYSTEM
stories.summary: A publicly released proof-of-concept, dubbed ShieldBreak, claims to bypass a previous Microsoft Defender patch and obtain SYSTEM privileges. Microsoft had not confirmed a new CVE at the time of reporting, so treat the claim as researcher-reported pending vendor confirmation, and monitor for tampering with Defender components.

stories.headline: Cisco ASA and FTD flaw exploited in the wild to trigger remote denial of service
stories.summary: A flaw in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software lets an unauthenticated attacker crash the device remotely. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August; NVD scores it 8.6 (HIGH). Patch or disable the affected VPN service on internet-facing firewalls.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: Microsoft patches 398 flaws, including a Windows driver zero-day under active attack
stories.summary: August's Patch Tuesday fixed 398 vulnerabilities, among them a Windows driver zero-day already being exploited - the WinSock AFD use-after-free (CVE-2026-68820) subsequently tied to Lazarus and added to CISA KEV. This is an unusually large rollup; prioritise the KEV-listed items.

stories.headline: Zoom annotation flaws could let one meeting participant hijack another's client
stories.summary: Vulnerabilities in Zoom's annotation feature allow a participant in a meeting to take control of another attendee's client. Update Zoom desktop clients; the attack requires only that the target join a meeting with the attacker.

stories.headline: Sandworm-linked UAC-0145 uses fake job interviews to push a trojanised WireGuard client
stories.summary: The Sandworm-linked cluster UAC-0145 is luring IT professionals with fake job interviews and delivering a trojanised WireGuard VPN client capable of running arbitrary commands. Verify VPN client installers against vendor checksums and treat interview-supplied software as hostile.

stories.headline: Researchers disclose an AI-assisted SharePoint exploit chain reaching unauthenticated RCE
stories.summary: A research team used AI tooling to assemble a SharePoint exploit chain that reaches unauthenticated remote code execution, published alongside the authentication-bypass work now being exploited. It is a further argument for getting SharePoint servers off the public internet.

stories.headline: DeadLock ransomware uses Polygon smart contracts to resist infrastructure takedown
stories.summary: DeadLock stores command-and-control addressing in Polygon smart contracts, so its infrastructure cannot be seized or sinkholed the way a domain or hosting account can. Detection has to shift to endpoint behaviour rather than blocklists.

stories.headline: A malicious SIM card can run attacker code inside cellular IoT modems
stories.summary: Researchers showed that a specially crafted SIM can execute code inside the baseband modems used by cellular IoT devices, below the level any host-side security control can see. There is no patch path for most affected devices; control physical access to SIM slots and source SIMs from trusted suppliers.

stories.headline: Mozilla revokes Firefox and Thunderbird Linux signing key after it leaked into a private repo
stories.summary: Mozilla revoked the signing key used for Firefox and Thunderbird Linux packages after discovering it had been committed to a private repository. Linux users and distribution maintainers need to refresh trusted keys so package verification keeps working.

stories.headline: 'Plug and Pwn': fake USB devices abuse auto-install for full SYSTEM takeover on Windows 11
stories.summary: Researchers turned Windows 11's automatic driver installation for newly attached USB devices into a full SYSTEM compromise using a spoofed device. Enforce USB device-installation policy via Group Policy on machines where physical access is a realistic threat.

stories.headline: Malicious MCP servers can split instructions to make AI coding agents exfiltrate secrets
stories.summary: A hostile Model Context Protocol server can fragment an instruction across multiple tool responses so that an AI coding agent assembles and executes it, exfiltrating credentials from the developer's environment. Pin MCP servers to trusted sources and scope the secrets an agent can reach.

stories.headline: Gunra ransomware exploits Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy flaws to breach networks
stories.summary: The Gunra ransomware operation is chaining known FortiOS and FortiProxy vulnerabilities for initial access. Fortinet edge devices remain one of the most reliably exploited entry points; confirm firmware is current and review VPN account activity.

stories.headline: Hackers breached a Polish power plant's controls via a private cellular network and shut a turbine
stories.summary: Attackers reached operational-technology controls at a Polish power plant through its private cellular network and shut down a turbine. The route bypassed the IT-network monitoring the operator relied on, which is the wider lesson for any site running private LTE or 5G alongside OT.

stories.headline: BdThemes supply-chain attack poisons JSON to create rogue WordPress admins
stories.summary: A compromise of BdThemes delivered poisoned JSON that silently creates administrator accounts on WordPress sites running its plugins. Audit the user list on affected sites and remove unrecognised admin accounts before updating.

stories.headline: China-linked hackers deploy new StormEncryptor ransomware, likely via an N-central flaw
stories.summary: A China-linked group is deploying ransomware tracked as StormEncryptor, with initial access believed to come from the N-able N-central authentication-bypass flaws that CISA added to its exploited catalog on 3 and 4 August (CVE-2026-18577 and CVE-2026-18556). N-able has shipped Hotfix 2; MSPs running N-central should verify it is applied.
